instruction: Change the font of the title text on the first slide to 'Liberation Mono'.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to change all text fonts to Liberation Sans Narrow via master slide editing. Spent 50 turns editing individual template elements in master slide view and tried Find & Replace, but failed to change fonts across all text boxes.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Impress UI, enter master slide view, select text, change font properties in Character panel, use keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl+H
metadata.failure_analysis: Model edited master slide template elements one-by-one instead of using a bulk method. Got confused between font variants. Find & Replace cannot change fonts. Task limit reached at 50 turns.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed the original 'change all fonts' task to a single font change on one text box. Model demonstrated ability to select text and change font name in the Character panel, so changing one title's font should be achievable.
metadata.explanation: Task requires selecting the title text on slide 1 and changing its font to Liberation Mono. Evaluator reads the pptx, finds the title placeholder on slide 1, and checks if all text runs use Liberation Mono font. Partial credit if some runs match.

scoring_breakdown.font_match: Partial credit: (matching_runs / total_runs). 1.0 if all title text runs use Liberation Mono.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the pptx file from VM, opens slide 0 (first slide), and finds the title placeholder by checking placeholder_format.idx for 0 (TITLE) or 15 (CENTER_TITLE).
Getter extracts font names from all text runs in the title, which is the correct granularity for verifying font changes.
Metric correctly handles the 'rule' expected type by directly accessing expected.get('expected_font') without unwrapping.
Case-insensitive font name comparison is appropriate and robust.
Partial credit scoring (matching_runs / total_runs) is reasonable for this task.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before evaluation to ensure changes are persisted to disk.

Minor concern: runs where run.font.name is None (theme-inherited fonts) are excluded from font_names list. If a title has mixed explicit/inherited runs, only explicitly-set fonts are checked. However, when a user changes the font of selected text in LibreOffice, all runs should get explicit font names in the saved pptx.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider handling runs with run.font.name = None by counting them as non-matching to ensure complete coverage, or add a fallback to check the paragraph-level or placeholder-level default font.
